label: A passive pointer in existing code-search guidance is the lowest-cost discoverability option, while external projects must opt in to UTCP configuration or install Sweet Search themselves.

Code Mode can expose Sweet Search through a UTCP manual, but Sweet Search documents its own --mcp setup through native .mcp.json registration, so a Code Mode manual and host runtime registration remain separate setup.

A new mcp-tooling mode or automatic system-spec-kit retrieval hook has higher routing and maintenance cost than a passive code-search pointer because those hubs have registered modes, router stages, resource maps and generated manifests, while system-spec-kit already routes document lookup and literal identifiers.
The doctor currently separates read-only Skilled install guidance from Code Mode MCP installation; a Sweet Search doctor route would add a second lifecycle alongside Sweet Search init and uninstall.

Sweet Search requires global package setup and a separate index for each project; model footprint and platform support vary, updates are incremental, stale version indexes require rebuilding, and the full first-index duration and total index storage remain unknown.
